LESSON: WRITING 2.4.1 PRE-WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: Writing 2.4.1 Pre-writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 2.4.1 Pre-writing, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: How do we sit when writing? 2. How do we write?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 2.4.1 Pre-writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Creativity and imagination: learner explores and undertakes tasks that require first -hand experience as they draw and colour different shapes.

Values:
Love: is enhanced as the learner shares with peers drawing and colouring materials.

Link to Pertinent Contemporary Issues:

Life skills: Self-esteem is enhanced as learners demonstrate and practise the correct body posture in preparation for writing.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Kiswahili Language Activities: as learners relate to the correct body posture while writing.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital devices

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
